title: Dzongu, Lachen and Lachung in seven nights from Siliguri
summary: A slower North Sikkim trip from Siliguri: two nights with a Lepcha family in Dzongu, then Lachen, Gurudongmar and two nights in Lachung, with Gangtok at each end. The low-altitude start helps your body adjust before the high lakes.
meta_description: Seven-night North Sikkim trip from NJP or Bagdogra: Gangtok, Dzongu Lepcha homestays, Lachen, Gurudongmar, Lachung and Yumthang. Plan and prices.
intro: Most North Sikkim trips are a rush from Gangtok and back. This one takes a week and adds Dzongu, the Lepcha reserve below Mangan, where you stay with a family, eat home food and walk between villages at a gentle 1,000–1,600 m. Then you go up to Lachen for Gurudongmar Lake and across to Lachung for Yumthang.

The order matters. Two nights low in Dzongu and a shorter drive to Lachen mean less time in the car on the day you go high. It suits Indian travellers who want both the lakes and the village life. Foreign travellers can follow it too, but must skip Gurudongmar and Zero Point and may add a second night in Lachung instead.
highlights: Two nights with a Lepcha family in Dzongu, with village and cardamom walks.
A shorter drive to Lachen from Dzongu than from Gangtok.
Gurudongmar Lake at about 5,430 m at dawn.
Yumthang valley and, for Indian travellers, snow at Zero Point.
A night in Gangtok at each end to absorb delays.

days.title: Siliguri to Gangtok
days.text: Arrive at NJP or Bagdogra and drive up the Teesta valley to Gangtok. Foreign nationals obtain the Sikkim Inner Line Permit at Rangpo or in advance. Hand your ID and photographs to your operator for the North Sikkim permit, and send copies to your Dzongu host if not done already. Evening on MG Marg.

days.title: Gangtok to Dzongu
days.text: Drive north through Kabi and Phodong to Mangan, then cross the Teesta into Dzongu. Your host meets you and settles you into a Lepcha homestay at around 1,000–1,600 m. Spend the afternoon walking around the village and meeting the family. Dinner by the kitchen fire, with stories about Kangchenjunga and the Lepcha past.

days.title: Village and cardamom walks in Dzongu
days.text: A full day on foot with a local guide: trails through big cardamom groves, orange orchards and bamboo, suspension bridges over side streams, and a waterfall or a neighbouring village. Birdwatchers should go out at first light. In the evening, rest and enjoy a slow dinner. This easy day also lets your body settle before the high valleys.

days.title: Dzongu to Lachen
days.text: Your operator's registered vehicle, arranged with the North Sikkim permit, collects you at Mangan or your homestay. Drive north along the Teesta to Chungthang and up the Lachen river to Lachen at about 2,750 m. Arriving earlier than Gangtok groups, you have time for a walk to Lachen Monastery. Eat lightly and sleep early.

days.title: Gurudongmar Lake and on to Lachung
days.drive: 134 km return to the lake, then about 50 km to Lachung; 10–12 hours
days.text: Leave at about 4 am, stop for tea at Thangu and reach Gurudongmar Lake at about 7–8 am. Spend 30–45 minutes at the shore and the shrine, walking slowly. Return to Lachen for breakfast, then drive via Chungthang to Lachung. Foreign travellers skip the lake and drive to Lachung at a gentler hour.

days.title: Yumthang valley and Zero Point
days.drive: About 94 km return with Zero Point, 6–7 hours
days.text: Leave Lachung at 6 am for Yumthang valley and its rhododendrons or snow. Indian travellers can carry on to Zero Point for an extra charge. Return via the hot spring. In the afternoon walk through the old village across the river or up to Lachung Monastery.

days.title: Lachung to Gangtok
days.text: Drive back down to Gangtok with stops at Bhim Nala, Naga falls and Mangan. Arrive in the late afternoon. This night in Gangtok gives you a buffer if the road is slow and a chance for a proper hot shower and a meal out.

days.title: Gangtok to Siliguri
days.text: Drive down to NJP or Bagdogra for your onward train or flight. Leave by 9 am for afternoon departures, and allow extra time in the monsoon or if there are works on the highway near the Teesta.

faqs.a: Dzongu sits low, around 1,000–1,600 m, so you rest after the drive from Siliguri and enjoy a slower pace before going high. It is also much closer to Lachen than Gangtok is, which shortens the drive on the day before Gurudongmar. And it shows a different side of North Sikkim: Lepcha village life.

faqs.q: How does the permit work when starting from Dzongu?
faqs.a: Your Gangtok operator applies for the North Sikkim permit with your ID while you are in Dzongu, and sends a registered vehicle to collect you at Mangan or the homestay. Your Dzongu host arranges the separate Dzongu permit. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

Mostly. Foreigners need an Inner Line Permit and a Protected Area Permit through a registered agent, in a group of two or more. They can visit Dzongu, Lachen, Lachung and Yumthang, but not Gurudongmar or Zero Point. A second Lachung night or more time in Dzongu fills the gap.

faqs.q: Is this trip suitable for families?
faqs.a: Dzongu, Lachung and Yumthang suit healthy families well. Gurudongmar is not advised for babies and young children; one parent can stay in Lachen with them while others go. The week-long pace with a rest day in Dzongu makes it easier than the short packages.

April to early June and October to November. In spring you get rhododendrons at Yumthang and flowers in Dzongu; in autumn clear skies and the cardamom harvest. Avoid June to September for landslides and leeches, and expect road closures to Gurudongmar from December to March.

faqs.q: How much does the seven-night trip cost?
faqs.a: Indicatively, about ₹21,500 per person on the Budget tier with homestays and shared transport, ₹37,500 per person for two with a reserved car and good hotels, and ₹59,000 with the best rooms and Zero Point. Prices are per person, twin sharing.

faqs.q: What if roads close during the trip?
faqs.a: The two Gangtok nights give you a buffer. If Lachen is closed, the operator may extend Dzongu or Lachung or swap Gurudongmar for an extra day elsewhere. Discuss changes and refunds before you pay, and keep a spare day before your flight.

faqs.q: How hard are the Dzongu walks?
faqs.a: Easy to moderate, on village paths with some steep stairs and river crossings on bridges. Your guide adjusts the route to your fitness. Good walking shoes, a water bottle and a rain jacket are enough for most of the year.

Yes. Add a second night in Lachen to make Gurudongmar easier, a third night in Dzongu for Tholung Monastery, or continue from Gangtok to West Sikkim or Darjeeling. Tell your operator early so permits and vehicles match your dates.
